papers.title_en: Where Tree Ensembles Decide: Structural Local Explanation with Decision Predicate Graphs
papers.evidence: 树集成预测的结构化局部解释方法
papers.tldr: 树集成预测虽准，但计算分散在大量规则中，现有归因与反事实难指出预测依赖哪些阈值。作者提出局部决策谓词图local DPG，将样本执行规则汇成可验证记录，并选出临界谓词及共享阈值的树。在16个数据集、4类集成模型上，它比随机和最近阈值谓词更好区分异预测邻居；单次跨越可在46%–69%错误预测中恢复真实类，优于TreeSHAP首选特征的29%–50%。该法无需外部解释器，为归因和反事实补充阈值级“可在哪里改变预测”。
papers.abstract_en: Tree ensembles are among the most accurate models for tabular data, yet the computation behind a single prediction is spread over hundreds of decision rules. Feature attributions and counterfactuals explain such predictions through the influence of features or a change of the input, leaving open which of the thresholds applied by the trees a prediction responds to, while structural explanations compress these rules and lose the trees behind them. To address this gap, we propose a local Decision Predicate Graph (local DPG), which gathers the rules executed for a sample into a verifiable record of the computation, with a class support that reproduces every explained prediction. From these rules we select the critical predicate, the executed predicate whose crossing is estimated to move the model most strongly toward a chosen class, which offers the user a concrete threshold and the trees that share it, without an external explainer. Across 16 datasets and four ensemble families, it separates differently predicted neighbours better than random and nearest-threshold predicates. A single crossing recovers the true class in 46-69% of wrong predictions, against 29-50% when the same rule is applied to the feature ranked first by TreeSHAP, a measure close to the selection criterion, and on planted faults it finds the faulty threshold in 46-71% of the resulting errors, against 6-21% at random. Although training-free edits of these predicates did not reduce the error on unseen data, the critical predicate complements attributions and counterfactuals by naming where a prediction can be changed.

papers.title_en: HeteroWear: Sensor-Aware Self-Supervised Learning for Heterogeneous Wearable Activity Recognition
papers.evidence: 面向异构可穿戴惯性与生理信号的自监督学习
papers.tldr: 可穿戴自监督学习常受限于单一数据集或设备，跨异构传感器配置的迁移性及预训练增益来源仍不明确。HeteroWear以传感器上下文嵌入、时序与跨传感器Transformer及潜在交叉注意力融合，分离传感器内时序建模与跨传感器关系建模，并结合结构化传感器丢弃、跨配置一致性和逐轴掩码传感器建模，在八数据集语料上预训练。留一数据集与受试者不重叠评估中，宏F1从0.688提升至0.724，HHAR达0.823，五基准中四个最优；留出设备提升0.066，50%通道移除仍保留73.8%性能。结果表明传感器感知预训练可跨异构配置迁移，并提升缺失通道鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Self-supervised learning for wearable sensing is usually confined to a single dataset or device family, leaving open whether representations transfer across heterogeneous sensor configurations and whether gains come from pretraining rather than architecture or richer sensor input. We present HeteroWear, a sensor-aware self-supervised framework pretrained on an eight-dataset wearable corpus (173 subjects, 358,261 windows) spanning inertial and physiological signals across body locations, devices, and sampling rates. HeteroWear separates within-sensor temporal modeling from cross-sensor relational modeling using sensor-context embeddings, temporal and cross-sensor Transformers, and latent cross-attention fusion. Training combines structured sensor dropout, cross-configuration consistency, and per-axis masked sensor modeling; missing sensors are omitted rather than reconstructed. Under leave-one-dataset-out pretraining and subject-disjoint evaluation on PAMAP2, WISDM, HHAR, HARTH, and UCI-HAR, HeteroWear improves mean macro-F1 from 0.688 to 0.724 over the identical architecture trained from scratch, with the largest gain on HHAR (0.823 versus 0.741), and achieves the highest macro-F1 on four of five benchmarks relative to single-accelerometer supervised baselines. Held-out-device evaluation yields a mean +0.066 macro-F1 improvement. Under 50% test-time channel removal, HeteroWear retains 73.8% of full-channel performance versus 64.1% for the same architecture trained from scratch without sensor dropout. Ablations show that structured sensor dropout primarily drives robustness, while cross-configuration consistency and sensor-context encoding contribute to transfer.
